items.actClause: AN ACT to authorize and direct the commissioner of agriculture and markets to study and develop a long-term strategy for sustaining farming and food production in New York state
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2479

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to authorize and direct the commissioner of
agriculture and markets to study and develop a long-term strategy for
sustaining farming and food production in New York state

 PURPOSE :

To authorize and direct the Commissioner to assess the effectiveness
of certain provisions of law meant to protect against encroachment by
development on to productive land, and to ensure agriculture's
statewide vitality. The Commissioner is further directed to examine
certain emerging agricultural practices and business models,
particularly those that could be utilized by small to mid-sized farms,
to determine how they might be encouraged in New York State.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

The Commissioner of the State Department of Agriculture and Markets is
given one year to produce a report for the Governor and Legislature,
which will describe a statewide blueprint for conserving productive
land and maintaining the vitality of agricultural production in New
York State. The Commissioner is directed to give particular focus to
article 25-AA, section 300 et seq., of the Agriculture and Markets
law. The Commissioner is further directed to propose programs that
encourage the growth of certain emerging trends and practices that
might benefit small to mid-sized farms.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The socio-economic vitality of agriculture in New York State is
essential to the economic stability and growth of many local
communities, and New York State as a whole. The study commissioned by
this bill will help to conserve, protect, and encourage the
development of productive agricultural businesses by examining two
things: how we currently protect productive land, and how we can
energize the businesses that depend on it. In particular, the
blueprint commissioned by this bill will address criticisms concerning
the functionality of critical statutory protections for farmland, and
will suggest programs that can propel the majority of New York State's
farmers in innovative new directions. The blueprint will help guide
policymakers towards options that will make New York State's farmers
more secure on their land, and in their businesses, for years to come.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New Bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Minimal.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Authorizes and directs the commissioner of agriculture and markets to study and develop a long-term strategy for sustaining farming and food production in New York state.
